g.title: ROS_QSP
g.text: follicular unit · TRPV1-CGRP neurovascular tone · VEGF angiogenesis · Th17 infiltrate · phyma fibrosis · ocular surface · drug PK/PD · clinical endpoints
one amplifier, four effector states with four different time constants — a drug's endpoint profile is decided by WHICH state it reads, not by how potent it is.
STATE 1 tone (minutes) · STATE 2 vessel structure (months) · STATE 3 infiltrate (weeks) · STATE 4 fibrosis (years, irreversible)

g.title: cluster_trig
g.text: patient-reported flush provocateurs — enter the model as one scalar TRIGGER load

g.title: cluster_cell
g.text: mast cell is the hub: it is downstream of LL-37 via MRGPRX2 AND upstream of both vessels and fibrosis

g.title: cluster_neuro
g.text: 5. Neurovascular axis — STATE 1 tone (tau ~ minutes) + TRPV1 sensitisation MEMORY
the only loop in the map that no licensed rosacea drug interrupts — which is why flush FREQUENCY survives treatment

g.title: cluster_barrier
g.text: the pH/protease layer that decides how much LL-37 gets made from a fixed amount of precursor

g.title: cluster_micro
g.text: , its bacteria, and the sebaceous habitat
density 0.7/cm2 healthy vs 10-15/cm2 papulopustular (standardised skin surface biopsy)

g.title: cluster_innate
g.text: 3. Innate immune amplifier — KLK5 · cathelicidin · LL-37 · TLR2 · NLRP3
: rosacea skin carries ~10x LL-37 and abnormal KLK5 processing; two positive feedback loops live here

g.title: cluster_vasc
g.text: 6. Vascular structure & angiogenesis — STATE 2 (tau ~ weeks-months, has MEMORY)
the substrate of PERSISTENT erythema: what an alpha-agonist cannot blanch and only a laser can remove

g.title: cluster_phyma
g.text: the one state with hysteresis: removing the drivers does not run it backwards, so only surgery/ablation moves it

g.title: cluster_ocul
g.text: 8. Ocular rosacea — the same amplifier at the lid margin
present in 50-75% of rosacea and poorly correlated with cutaneous severity;

g.title: cluster_pktop
g.text: 9. Topical drug PK — skin depot kinetics
vehicle -> stratum corneum reservoir -> viable epidermis/dermis -> follicular (sebaceous) compartment

g.title: cluster_pksys
g.text: doxycycline 40 mg modified-release is deliberately SUB-antimicrobial (Cmax ~0.6 mg/L, below MIC) — anti-protease only

g.title: cluster_pd
g.text: 11. Target engagement — WHICH STATE does each drug read?
the alpha-2A adaptation pair (receptor availability + compensatory vasodilator drive) is what generates rebound erythema

g.title: cluster_dev
g.text: 12. Physical modalities — the only tools that DELETE a state
selective photothermolysis empties STATE 2; ablative/surgical work is the only exit from STATE 4

g.title: cluster_end
g.text: each endpoint is wired to ONE state — which is how the map predicts endpoint-specific drug failure

g.title: cluster_com
g.text: shared low-grade innate inflammation and the neurovascular phenotype turn up outside the skin

g.title: LEG1
g.text: STATE 1 tone .......... minutes, no memory -> flushing, blanchable erythema
STATE 2 vessel density weeks-months, memory -> persistent erythema, telangiectasia
STATE 3 infiltrate ..... weeks, memory ...... -> papules, pustules

g.title: LEG2
g.text: WHICH STATE DOES THE DRUG READ?

g.title: LEG3
g.text: L1 LL-37 -> TLR2 -> KLK5 -> LL-37 (innate amplification)
L2 KLK5 -> IL-1beta -> MMP-9 -> KLK5 (protease amplification)
L4 flush -> TRPV1 up -> lower threshold -> flush (progression ETR -> fixed)
plus oedema <-> lymphatic stasis (phyma) and DLQI -> stress -> CRH -> mast cell

g.title: LEG4
g.text: 1. doxycycline lowers lesions across a 10-fold dose range while mite density
stays nearly flat -- anti-protease, not acaricidal
2. brimonidine gives the largest day-1 CEA drop of any agent and the
largest week-8 rebound in the subgroup with fast alpha-2A desensitisation
3. an agent that only clears Demodex delays RELAPSE more than it speeds RESPONSE
4. laser improves CEA without touching ILC; ivermectin the reverse
5. no pharmacotherapy in this map reduces flush FREQUENCY below the
trigger-driven floor set by TRPV1 sensitisation
